references.text: In the time of the Judges, each man did what was right in his own eyes, reflecting the same state of spiritual disorder warned against in Deuteronomy 12:8
The conclusion of the book of Judges repeats that everyone did what was right in their own eyes, a direct parallel to the warning in Deuteronomy 12:8
Proverbs warns against following one's own way, which seems right in one's own eyes, but the fool does not listen to advice
Every man's way is right in his own eyes, but the Lord tests the hearts - the same theme of human self-deception
Israel was commanded not to follow their own heart and eyes, but to remember the Lord's commands - a parallel warning against self-rule
